short: The quarterly statement a deductor files reporting tax deducted and deposited.
seoTitle: TDS Return — Meaning, Due Dates and Late Fee
metaDescription: A TDS return is the quarterly statement a deductor files reporting the tax deducted, the payees and the challans used, so credit reaches the right taxpayer.
definition: A TDS return is the quarterly statement a deductor files with the income tax department, reporting the tax deducted during the quarter, who it was deducted from, and the challans through which it was deposited — the filing that makes the credit visible to the person it was deducted from.
bodyHtml:
Why the return matters as much as the deposit

Depositing tax gets the money to the government. The return is what allocates it. Until a deductee appears in a filed return against a valid PAN, the deduction does not show in their tax credit statement, and they cannot claim it. A deposit without a return creates a dispute with your own vendor or employee.

Quarterly due dates

  • April to June: 31 July
  • July to September: 31 October
  • October to December: 31 January
  • January to March: 31 May

Separate returns for separate payments

Salary deductions and non-salary deductions to residents are reported on different statements, and payments to non-residents on another. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 the form numbering was reworked alongside the section numbering, so the label shown on the filing portal may differ from the one used in earlier years — file from what the portal currently presents.

Cost of filing late

A late fee runs per day of delay, capped at the amount of tax deducted, with a further penalty possible where the return is not filed within the permitted window. Corrections are possible after filing, but each revision delays the credit reaching the deductee.

faq.question: What happens if I deposit TDS but never file the return?
faq.answer: The money sits with the government unallocated. The deductee cannot see or claim the credit, and a daily late fee accrues until the return is filed, capped at the tax deducted.

faq.question: Can a TDS return be revised?
faq.answer: Yes. Corrections to details such as a wrong PAN or a misquoted challan can be filed, but each revision delays credit reaching the deductee, so it is cheaper to collect PAN accurately at onboarding.
